bai.ten: The photoelectric effect: measuring the energy of light
bai.moTa: Change the colour, count electrons and use a retarding voltage to measure kinetic energy.
bai.yChinh: Light transfers energy in quanta. For a given surface, frequency determines the maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons. Changing the number of incident photons per second changes the emission rate.
bai.giaiThich: Light transfers energy in quanta. For a given surface, frequency determines the maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons. Changing the number of incident photons per second changes the emission rate.
bai.hieuDung: Electrons may lose energy inside the metal. The model tracks the fastest electrons travelling perpendicular to the plates to find the stopping potential. The spheres and their motion illustrate absorption and flight on enlarged scales.
bai.nguon: Trí Lữ · OpenStax, University Physics, Vol. 3, §6.2 · NIST CODATA 2022.
bai.baiGiang.mucTieu.1: Find a cathode's threshold by varying frequency.
bai.baiGiang.mucTieu.2: Distinguish photon flux from the energy of a single photon.
bai.baiGiang.mucTieu.3: Infer maximum kinetic energy and work function from stopping voltage.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.1.noiDung:
A light pulse goes from the source to the metal. When an electron reaches the collector you hear a click. Follow one pulse through the apparatus. The dot outside the metal represents an electron; the incoming flash represents a photon. The electron was already in the metal before the light arrived.

Distinguish the two counters. The source count rises when a photon leaves. The collector count rises only after an electron crosses the gap. The delay on screen illustrates flight time; it does not represent a delay while the electron accumulates energy inside the metal.

$$E_\gamma=hf$$

+++ Explore further · Follow one absorption event

$E_\gamma$ denotes photon energy, $f$ light frequency and $h$ Planck’s constant. A beam can carry a great deal of energy, but in a single-photon experiment an absorbing electron receives the whole energy of exactly one photon, one quantum $hf$, at a time.

+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Send one photon|mot]]
bai.baiGiang.buoc.2.ten: How much energy does a photon carry?
bai.baiGiang.buoc.2.noiDung:
This step opens with orange light at about 500 THz. Switch to a higher frequency. The source colour shows the change; violet represents frequencies beyond the visible spectrum. Read the frequency on the control. At higher frequencies each photon carries more energy, and its vacuum wavelength is shorter.

Watch the gold point on the graph before and after changing colour. The horizontal axis shows frequency, the vertical axis the maximum kinetic energy after the electron escapes. They can be measured independently. The brightness of an on-screen dot does not measure photon energy.

$$\lambda=c/f$$

+++ Explore further · How much energy does a photon carry?

At $600\,\mathrm{THz}$, a photon carries about $2{,}48\,\mathrm{eV}$ and its wavelength is nearly $500\,\mathrm{nm}$. An electronvolt is the energy an elementary charge gains across a potential difference of one volt.

+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Set 600 THz|chon]]
bai.baiGiang.buoc.3.noiDung:
Photons reach the cathode, but the collector is silent. The metal confines its electrons behind an energy barrier. The work function is the minimum energy required to remove an electron from the Fermi level to just outside the surface. Below threshold, sending more photons still releases no electrons in this single-photon model.

Increase flux below threshold and watch the collector. Then change only the frequency until it crosses threshold. These two tests distinguish a limit on each photon’s energy from a limit on the total energy delivered in a second.

$$f_0=\frac{W}{h}$$

+++ Explore further · Each surface has a threshold

The model cathode has work function $W=2\,\mathrm{eV}$. Its threshold is about $484\,\mathrm{THz}$. At threshold the maximum kinetic energy is zero; raise the frequency a little more for electrons to cross the gap.

+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Try below threshold|thu]]
bai.baiGiang.buoc.3.thuThach.de: Drag the frequency control until electrons just escape with maximum kinetic energy between 0.03 and 0.09 eV.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.3.thuThach.goiY: Find the threshold for the 2 eV cathode, then raise the frequency a little.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.4.noiDung:
Keep frequency fixed and watch the flashes at the cathode. Doubling the flux doubles the incoming photons in a fixed interval. If emission and collection efficiencies stay constant, the photocurrent increases proportionally. The colour and maximum electron energy stay the same.

Keep the retarding voltage at zero so the field does not reject electrons. If the observation intervals differ, raw counts cannot be compared directly; divide the number of electrons collected by the observation time.

$$I=e\eta\dot N_\gamma$$

+++ Explore further · Increase flux at constant frequency

Here $I$ is the saturation current, $e$ the magnitude of the electron charge, $\eta$ the quantum efficiency and $\dot N_\gamma$ the number of photons arriving per second. In a real tube the saturation current is measured with the collector slightly positive so that every emitted electron is gathered; here the voltage is zero and every model electron flies straight to the collector. Clicks represent detections; at high rates only a fraction sound.

+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Double the flux|doi]]
bai.baiGiang.buoc.5.noiDung:
A photon gives its energy to an electron. Part of that energy pays the work function needed to escape. For the fastest electron the remainder is its maximum kinetic energy. An electron starting deep in the metal may lose more energy on the way out.

The gold point moves along the line for the selected cathode. Part of the photon energy is needed to take an electron across the surface even with no applied voltage. Using the whole photon energy as the electron’s outgoing kinetic energy would omit that cost.

$$K_{\max}=hf-W\quad (f\ge f_0)$$

+++ Explore further · The fastest electron’s energy budget

For a $W=2\,\mathrm{eV}$ cathode and $600\,\mathrm{THz}$ light, the maximum kinetic energy is about $0{,}48\,\mathrm{eV}$. Raising the frequency to $800\,\mathrm{THz}$ with the same cathode gives about $1{,}31\,\mathrm{eV}$. The difference comes from the change in photon energy.

+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Raise 600 to 800 THz|tang]]
bai.baiGiang.buoc.6.ten: Slow electrons with an electric field
bai.baiGiang.buoc.6.noiDung:
The collector is held below the cathode potential. The electric field slows an electron travelling towards it. Raise the retarding voltage to see an electron stop and turn back. Lower the voltage and it reaches the collector again.

Watch the turning position as well as the counter. In a uniform field the work done against the electric force is proportional to the distance travelled. At higher reverse voltage the electron spends its kinetic energy sooner. Clicks stop when electrons no longer reach the collector.

$$eU_s=K_{\max}$$

+++ Explore further · Slow electrons with an electric field

An electron loses energy $eU$ crossing the full gap. The photocurrent just vanishes when this equals the fastest electron’s initial kinetic energy. Kinetic energy in electronvolts and stopping potential in volts then have the same numerical value.

+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Set the retarding voltage to 0.30 V|ham]]
bai.baiGiang.buoc.6.thuThach.de: Drag the retarding voltage until the electrons turn back after crossing 75–85% of the gap.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.6.thuThach.goiY: The fractional turning distance equals the initial energy in eV divided by the retarding voltage in V.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.7.ten: Change the cathode, keep the source
bai.baiGiang.buoc.7.noiDung:
Select a model cathode with a larger work function. The same photon may release an electron from one surface yet carry too little energy for another. A threshold measurement therefore needs a specified material and surface condition.

The highlighted line is the selected cathode; the dim lines show the other two. Each line starts at its own emission threshold. The imaginary extension to negative values is used to infer the work function. No electron is emitted with negative kinetic energy.

$$K_{\max}=hf-W\quad (f\ge f_0)$$

+++ Explore further · Change the cathode, keep the source

At $800\,\mathrm{THz}$, changing the work function from $W=2\,\mathrm{eV}$ to $W=3\,\mathrm{eV}$ reduces the maximum kinetic energy by exactly $1\,\mathrm{eV}$ to about $0{,}31\,\mathrm{eV}$. Plotted against frequency, the two materials have the same slope $h$ and different intercepts on the frequency axis.

+++

> [Thử ngay] [[Use the 3 eV cathode|thay]]
bai.baiGiang.buoc.7.thuThach.de: Drag the frequency until electrons from the 3 eV cathode have maximum kinetic energy between 0.45 and 0.55 eV.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.7.thuThach.goiY: Add the work function to the desired kinetic energy to obtain the photon energy.
bai.baiGiang.buoc.8.noiDung:
In the laboratory the stopping voltage is found by adjusting the voltage until the photocurrent disappears. Repeat at different frequencies and use the slope to infer Planck’s constant. Extrapolated, the line meets the vertical axis at $-W$, so the intercept gives the work function; there is no photocurrent below threshold.

Record the frequency, cathode material and how you identified the disappearance of the current so someone else can check the reasoning. The model assumes a clean surface, monochromatic light and single-photon absorption.

$$\frac{\Delta K_{\max}}{\Delta f}=h$$

+++ Explore further · Work backwards from a measurement

Restore the first cathode and try $600\,\mathrm{THz}$ and $800\,\mathrm{THz}$. The difference in maximum kinetic energies is approximately $0{,}83\,\mathrm{eV}$. Taking the difference eliminates the work function from the slope calculation. At least two above-threshold measurements are needed.

+++

bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.1.hoi: If monochromatic light is below threshold, what happens when the photon flux doubles?
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.1.giai: Each single photon still has too little energy for escape.
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.2.hoi: Two sources illuminate the same cathode at the same frequency. Which gives a larger maximum kinetic energy?
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.2.giai: In the single-photon regime the photon energy minus the work function is the same.
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.3.hoi: Why does stopping voltage reveal maximum kinetic energy?
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.3.chon.1: The field stops even the fastest electron
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.3.giai: The photocurrent vanishes when even the fastest electron cannot reach the collector.
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.4.hoi: How does a change of cathode affect the maximum-energy versus frequency line?
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.4.chon.1: The slope changes but the threshold stays fixed
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.4.chon.2: The slope stays fixed but the threshold changes
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.4.giai: The slope is h, while the work function depends on the surface.
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.5.hoi: Why is a count of arriving electrons insufficient to infer a single photon’s energy?
bai.baiGiang.cauHoi.5.dap: Counts depend on flux and collection efficiency. Frequency or kinetic-energy information is needed to infer the photon energy.
